title: Did Congress Waste Warsh Hearings on AI While Inflation Runs Hot? Cato Blasts Focus on 'Trendy Topics'

New Federal Reserve Chairman Kevin Warsh faced Congress last week for the first time, but a Cato Institute economist says lawmakers may have squandered their best chance to press him before rates move.

In a commentary published Monday, Cato's Jai Kedia argued an outsized share of the questioning went to artificial intelligence, calling it "a poor use of scarce oversight time."

"That is the real cost of spending the hearings on trendy topics like artificial intelligence, while the issues that will shape policy this year went somewhat underexamined," Kedia wrote.

Warsh and Cook Split on AI Inflation

Pressed on whether massive AI investment may prove inflationary, Warsh said, "I don't view one change in prices as necessarily being inflationary," arguing supply would likely grow to catch up with demand, according to CNBC. He contrasted that with a foreign conflict, which he said tends to shrink the economy's supply side.

Not everyone at the Fed appears as relaxed.

Gov. Lisa Cook warned the same day that AI spending may drive significant price increases across chips, software and utilities, saying inflation risks now outweigh employment risks in her view. Warsh described the internal debate as "one of the good family fights."

The unresolved Iran conflict cuts the other way. Oil jumped more than 2% Tuesday on fresh attacks, with Brent back above $91, threatening the energy relief that drove June's cooling.

Funds like the United States Oil Fund, which tracks WTI, have swung on each ceasefire collapse. Kedia asks whether the Fed has concrete contingency plans for the war's outcomes, a question he says went unasked.

The Questions That Went Unasked

Kedia listed four underexamined issues: the near-term plan to return inflation to 2%, mixed labor signals, Iran-driven inflation risk, and whether higher interest payments on bank reserves could push the Fed back into operating losses.

Kedia argues the labor market's flat unemployment rate masks weakness, saying job growth has stagnated and the rate only holds steady because workers have left the labor force. Warsh's own testimony offered the opposite read, describing job creation as keeping pace with the workforce.

新任美联储主席凯文·沃什上周首次面对国会，但卡托研究所的一位经济学家表示，立法者可能已经浪费了在利率调整前向他施压的最佳机会。

在周一发表的一篇评论中，卡托的杰·凯迪亚认为，大部分问题都针对人工智能，称其“对稀缺监督时间的利用不当”。

凯迪亚写道：“这是在人工智能等流行话题上举行听证会的真正成本，而影响今年政策的问题却在某种程度上受到了低估。”

沃什和库克在人工智能通胀问题上存在分歧

据 CNBC 报道，当被问及大规模人工智能投资是否会导致通货膨胀时，沃什表示，“我不认为价格的任何变化都一定会导致通货膨胀”，他认为供应可能会增长以赶上需求。 他将其与外国冲突进行了对比，他表示外国冲突往往会收缩经济的供给面。

并非美联储的每个人都显得如此放松。

政府。 丽莎·库克（Lisa Cook）当天警告称，人工智能支出可能会推动芯片、软件和公用事业的价格大幅上涨，并表示在她看来，通胀风险现在超过了就业风险。 沃什将这场内部辩论描述为“一场精彩的家庭斗争”。

悬而未决的伊朗冲突则恰恰相反。 周二，油价因新的袭击而上涨超过 2%，布伦特原油价格回到 91 美元上方，威胁到推动 6 月份降温的能源缓解措施。

趋势：避免第一大投资错误：你的“安全”持仓可能会让你付出巨大的代价

追踪 WTI 的美国石油基金等基金在每次停火失败时都会发生波动。 凯迪亚询问美联储是否针对战争结果制定了具体的应急计划，他说这个问题没有被问到。

那些未被提出的问题

Kedia列出了四个未经充分审查的问题：将通胀率恢复到2%的近期计划、好坏参半的劳工信号、伊朗驱动的通胀风险，以及银行准备金支付更高的利息是否会导致美联储重新陷入运营亏损。

凯迪亚认为，劳动力市场持平的失业率掩盖了经济疲软，他表示，就业增长停滞，失业率之所以保持稳定，是因为工人离开了劳动力市场。 沃什自己的证词提供了相反的解读，他将就业创造描述为与劳动力保持同步。
